nodes: Believe you are free and you are. Believe you are bound and you are. As you think, so you become.
You are pure awareness, wider than any worry. Don't let your mind shrink into pettiness.
Be free of expectations, steady, self-reliant and cool at heart: deep, and impossible to rattle.
Treat craving like poison. Drink forgiveness, honesty, kindness, contentment and truth like nectar.
Step back from the body, rest as awareness, and right now you can be happy, calm and free.
You are not your caste, your stage of life, or what others can see. You are the witness. Be happy.
'Everything depends on me' is a snakebite. The antidote is trusting you are not the only doer.
Wherever craving lives, the treadmill runs. Let go of the craving, and be happy.
Money, pleasure, even good deeds: none of them ever gave this mind rest.
You have toiled so long with body, mind and speech. Now, at last, stop.
Things arise, change and end by their own nature. Seeing that, you can be at peace.
Good times and hard times arrive on their own schedule. Knowing that, you can stop longing and grieving.
Suffering is born of worry, nothing else. Free of worry, you are happy and at peace.
Even monks rarely find the ease of wanting nothing. I stopped grabbing and stopped renouncing, and live happily.
Do what comes to you to do, then let it go and live at ease.
A clear mind gets it from one plain teaching; a muddled one searches all its life.
Whether the body lasts a hundred years or ends today, what you are neither gains nor loses.
Let the waves of the world rise or fall. You, the ocean, neither gain nor lose.
Don't churn your mind with plans and second thoughts. Be still and rest in yourself.
Freedom is losing your taste for what hooks you; bondage is savouring it. That's all you need to know.
You are not your body or your achievements. You are the awareness watching it all. Live lightly.
Liking and disliking belong to the mind. You are not your mind.
Have faith, my child, have faith. You are more than everything that happens to you.
The body comes and goes; what you truly are does not. Why grieve so?
Read and recite all the scriptures you like; peace comes when you set them all down.
Pride in being spiritual is still pride. It only adds to your suffering.
Enjoy, work or meditate all you like: your heart still longs for the place where wanting stops.
Everyone suffers from constant straining, and no one notices. Seeing this alone brings peace.
Running away won't free you from pain. Free of clinging, you can be at peace right where you are.
Content, clear-minded and happy in your own company: that is the fruit of all practice.
Rare is the person who doesn't replay old pleasures or pine for new ones.
Not wishing life away, not resenting it, the blessed one lives happily on whatever comes.
A calm mind doesn't need the crowd or the forest. It is the same wherever it is.
Throne or begging bowl, gain or loss, crowd or solitude: a steady person stays the same.
You can earn everything and enjoy everything, and still not be happy until you let go.
Don't cling to doing or to not doing. Do what's in front of you and stay at ease.
When 'I still have to do this' burns you up inside, only a rain of calm brings relief.
Chasing calm keeps it away. Seeing clearly, the wise are calm without trying.
Even when family laughs at you or scolds you, you can stay unshaken inside.
A restless mind is agitated even doing nothing; a skilled one stays calm doing everything.
Sit, sleep, come, go, talk and eat at ease. Calm can live inside ordinary days.
A restless mind turns even rest into busyness. A still mind finds rest even in work.
Not begging for gain, not grieving loss: a steady mind stays cool and full.
Beggar or king: whoever is free of craving shines.
Free of craving, you stop replaying what you did and didn't do.
Praise doesn't inflate you, blame doesn't enrage you, death doesn't frighten you. That is freedom.
Wonder of wonders: I own nothing, and yet everything is mine.
If you know what in you can't be lost, why still chase more money?
Watch yourself as you'd watch anyone else, and praise or blame stops shaking you.
When the world's show stops dazzling you, even death close by loses its terror.
Even when every hope collapses, a mind that wants nothing stays whole.
Wanting nothing, you can take what comes your way without being thrilled or hurt.
You are the ocean these waves rise in. Why run around like a beggar for more?
Be the same in pain and pleasure, hope and despair. That evenness is freedom.
Bondage is a mind that wants, grieves, grabs and rages. Freedom is a mind that stops.
Where 'I' and 'mine' take over, you are bound. Hold things lightly; grab nothing, push nothing away.
Done and not done: has that list ever ended for anyone? Knowing this, ease your grip.
No age of life comes without ups and downs. Accept what comes and keep going.
Even the great sages disagree. Seeing that, who would keep fighting over opinions?
Mind, why are you running around like a lost ghost? Drop the clinging and be happy.
Friend mind, why all this chatter? It's all speculation. You are vast as the sky.
Take wisdom from anyone. Nobody throws away a jewel just because it fell in the mud.
An unpainted boat still carries you across. Look for substance, not polish.
Drop the likes and grudges, work for everyone's good, stay steady: that is the highest path.
Thoughts rise and burst like bubbles in water. You don't have to chase them.
Why weep, friend? What you truly are does not age, die or change.
Let go, and then let go of your pride in letting go.
Not chasing pleasure, not refusing it, he walks slowly, slowly, in natural joy.
Gentle, self-restrained, content with little, moderate in food, calm and steady: that is quiet strength.
Seek no honour for yourself, give it freely to others; stay alert, deep, friendly and kind.
Kind, harming no one, patient with everyone, truthful to the core, and helpful to all.
Free of the noose of expectation, he lives in joy from start to finish.
Let go of old cravings, speak only what heals, and live in the present.
Even Arjuna, the finest archer alive, froze when the fight was against his own people.
Shaking limbs, a dry mouth, a racing body: the Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero.
Arjuna put down his bow and sat in the chariot, too overwhelmed to go on.
Listen again. I am telling you this for your good, because you are dear to me.
Out of compassion, I live in their hearts and clear the darkness with the lamp of understanding.
I am the self seated in every heart: the beginning, middle and end of all beings.
Whatever shines with excellence, beauty or power, see it as a spark of the divine.
Their minds on me, they talk of me with each other, and find joy and contentment in it.
Seeing something too big to take in, my heart trembles and I can't find steadiness or calm.
It's already set in motion. Rise and do your part; be the instrument.
I treated you casually, as just a friend, never seeing how great you were.
For every careless joke, every time I took you for granted, alone or in company, forgive me.
Bear with me as a father bears with a son, a friend with a friend, a lover with the beloved.
I'm thrilled and terrified at once. Show me the familiar face again.
Don't be afraid or confused by what you've seen. Let the fear go and look again with a calm heart.
Seeing Arjuna frightened, Krishna took his gentle, familiar form again and comforted him.
Seeing your gentle human face again, I am calm. I feel like myself again.
By a love that looks nowhere else, I can truly be known, seen, and entered.
Work for the divine, love it, drop clinging, and hold no hatred towards any being.
If even practice is too hard, just do your work for my sake. That alone takes you far.
And if even that's beyond you, then simply let go of the results of what you do.
Practice is good, understanding better, meditation better still. But letting go of results brings peace at once.
Hate no one. Be friendly and kind, free of 'mine' and ego, steady in pain and joy, and forgiving.
Always content, self-disciplined, firm in resolve, heart and mind given to the divine: such a person is dear to me.
Unsettle no one, be unsettled by no one, free of elation, resentment, fear and agitation.
Wanting nothing extra, clean within and without, capable, unbothered, not chasing every new venture: dear to me.
Not swinging between thrill and hate, grief and craving, letting go of 'good' and 'bad' outcomes: dear to me.
The same to friend and foe, in respect and insult, heat and cold, pleasure and pain.
Praise and blame weigh the same. Quiet, content with what comes, rooted in steadiness, not status.
Those who rest their mind in me, always, with deep trust, I count as closest to me.
Senses in hand, even-minded everywhere, glad in the good of all beings: they reach me too.
Lay your work in me and keep your mind on me; I soon lift you out of the drowning sea.
Whoever rests their heart in me, I lift out of the drowning sea, and soon.
Rest your mind in me, settle your thinking in me, and you will live in me.
If you can't keep your mind fixed yet, then reach for it through regular practice.
Some find the truth by meditation, some by thinking it through, some by selfless work.
Others, not knowing these paths, learn by listening to others, and they too cross over.
Whoever sees the same undying presence in all beings, even as they perish, truly sees.
Seeing the divine equally everywhere, you stop wounding yourself through yourself.
Like the sky, untouched by everything that moves through it, the self stays unstained.
No need for status, no pretence, no harm, patience, straightness, respect for teachers, purity, steadiness, self-control.
Not chasing pleasures, not puffed up, and clear-eyed about birth, death, old age and illness.
When restlessness rules: greed, constant activity, starting project after project, craving and no peace.
When dullness rules: darkness, sluggishness, carelessness and confusion.
Don't hate your moods when they come, or long for them when they go.
Sit like a witness, unshaken, knowing it's just moods moving through, and stay steady.
Even in pain and pleasure, at ease in yourself; earth, stone and gold the same; praise and blame alike.
The same in respect and disrespect, to friend and foe, letting go of the need to start everything: free.
Dullness, born of ignorance, ties you down through carelessness, laziness and too much sleep.
I am seated in every heart. Memory, knowledge and their fading come from me.
Free of pride and delusion, past the pull of attachment, the steady reach what doesn't fade.
Every living being is an eternal part of me, says Krishna.
Fearlessness, a clean heart, steady learning, generosity, self-control, study and straightforwardness.
Clinging to worries that only end at death, they believe owning and enjoying is all there is.
Tied by a hundred ropes of hope, pushed by desire and anger, they pile up wealth by any means.
'I got this today, I'll get that next. This is mine, and more will be mine.' The mind of more.
'I'm rich, well-born; who else is like me?' So speaks the deluded mind.
Self-important, stubborn, drunk on money and status, they give for show.
No harm, truthfulness, no anger, no gossip, compassion for all, no greed, gentleness, modesty, no fidgeting.
Desire, anger and greed: three gates to self-ruin. Close all three.
Freed from these three dark gates, you do what's truly good for you and reach the highest.
Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, cleanliness, no malice, no arrogance: the marks of a good nature.
Show-off, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance: the marks of a nature heading the wrong way.
Good qualities free you; harsh ones bind. Don't worry; you were born with the good.
Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
A calm mind, gentleness, quiet, self-restraint and a clean heart: that is discipline of mind.
Effort made for respect, status or show is shaky and doesn't last.
Discipline done through stubborn self-torment, or to harm another, is the dark kind.
Give because giving is right, to someone who can't repay you, at the right time and place.
Giving to get something back, or giving grudgingly, isn't really giving.
You are made of what you deeply believe. As your faith is, so are you.
Food that builds life, strength, health, cheer and calm: that's the food of a clear mind.
The wise don't hate unpleasant work or cling to pleasant work. Doubts gone, they just do it.
No one with a body can give up action completely. Letting go of the payoff is the real renouncing.
Every result has five causes: the setting, the doer, the tools, the efforts, and the unseen. You're one of them.
If you think you alone made it happen, or alone made it fail, you're not seeing the whole picture.
Clear understanding sees one undivided life in all beings, though they appear separate.
Good action is steady, done without clinging, not driven by like or dislike, or by what you'll get.
Work done with huge strain, for ego or pleasure, is the restless kind.
Action begun in confusion, without weighing consequences, cost, harm or your own capacity, is dark action.
Free of clinging and boasting, full of resolve and enthusiasm, unchanged by success or failure: the best kind of doer.
Hungry for results, greedy, willing to harm, unclean, tossed by joy and grief: the restless kind of doer.
Careless, crude, stubborn, deceitful, spiteful, lazy, gloomy and always putting things off: the dull kind of doer.
Clear judgement knows when to act and when to wait, what to fear, and what frees you.
A mind clouded by restlessness can't quite tell right from wrong, or what to do from what to avoid.
A mind wrapped in darkness takes wrong for right and sees everything upside down.
True resolve holds mind, breath and senses steady through unwavering practice.
Clinging to duty, pleasure and wealth for what they'll bring you is restless resolve.
Stubbornly holding on to sleep, fear, grief, despair and pride is the dark kind of resolve.
There is a joy you grow into through practice, one that brings sorrow to an end.
Some joy tastes like poison at first and like nectar in the end. That joy is worth it.
Some pleasure tastes like nectar at first and poison in the end. Know which kind you're choosing.
Pleasure from sleep, laziness and carelessness dulls you from start to finish.
Devoted to your own work, you reach fulfilment. Here's how.
Doing your own work well can be your worship of the source of all life.
Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.
Unattached everywhere, self-mastered, free of craving: that's the highest freedom.
Let go of ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness. Without 'mine', you become peaceful.
Serene within, they neither grieve nor crave, and treat all beings alike.
Doing all their work while leaning on me, they reach the lasting home, by my grace.
Inwardly hand all your work to the divine, hold it as your goal, and keep your mind on it.
Heart turned to the divine, you'll cross every obstacle. Refuse out of ego, and you'll be lost.
Even good work should be done without clinging to it or its rewards. That's my settled view.
The divine lives in the heart of every being, yours included.
Take refuge in the divine with all your being. By that grace you'll find supreme peace.
I've told you all I know. Reflect on it fully, then do as you choose.
Listen once more to my deepest word: you are truly dear to me.
Mind on me, heart devoted to me, you will come to me. I promise: you are dear to me.
Lean on me alone. I will free you from every wrong. Don't worry.
Walking away from a real responsibility out of confusion is the darkest kind of letting go.
My confusion is gone, my clarity is back. I stand firm, free of doubt, and I'll act.
Where wisdom and skilled effort stand together, there is fortune, victory, wellbeing and steady justice.
Dropping a duty just because it's hard or you fear the strain isn't freedom. It gains you nothing.
Do what must be done because it must be done, letting go of clinging and the payoff.
You grieve for what doesn't need your grief, while talking like you know better.
There was never a time when you, I, or anyone here did not exist, and never will be.
Childhood, youth, old age: the body keeps changing. The wise aren't thrown by the next change.
Heat and cold, pleasure and pain come and go. They don't last; learn to bear them.
The one who stays the same in pain and pleasure, undisturbed by either, is ready for real freedom.
What is unreal never truly lasts; what is real never stops being.
The self was never born and never dies. It is not killed when the body is.
As we drop worn-out clothes and put on new ones, the self leaves a worn body for a new one.
No weapon cuts it, no fire burns it, no water wets it, no wind dries it.
It is unseen, beyond thought, unchanging. Knowing this, ease your grief.
Even if you believe life simply begins and ends, there's still no need to be crushed by grief.
Whatever is born will die, and what dies is born again. Don't torment yourself over the unavoidable.
We come from the unseen and return to it; only the middle is visible. Why break over that?
The self within every body can never be destroyed. So don't grieve for any creature as lost.
Hold pleasure and pain, gain and loss, win and defeat as equal. Then step in and act.
No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
A decided mind is single and focused. An undecided mind splits into endless branches.
Chasing comfort and power, the mind can never settle into a single purpose.
Rise above the pull of opposites. Stay centred, not obsessed with getting and keeping.
Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
Do the work steadily, letting go of clinging. Stay the same in success and failure; that balance is yoga.
Working only for the payoff makes you poor inside. Take shelter in clear understanding.
Yoga is skill in action: doing the work well, without being bound by it.
When your mind clears the fog, you'll tire of all you've heard and all you're yet to hear.
Pulled by conflicting advice, the mind wobbles. When it settles and stays still, you've arrived.
When you stop chasing every desire and find contentment within yourself, your wisdom becomes steady.
Unshaken in sorrow, not craving in joy, free of clinging, fear and anger: that is a steady mind.
Good news doesn't inflate them, bad news doesn't embitter them. That's steady wisdom.
Like a tortoise pulling in its limbs, draw your senses back from what pulls at them.
Staying away from a craving dims it, but the taste lingers until something higher replaces it.
I can't tell which is better, or even what winning would look like.
Even a wise, striving person can be dragged off by restless senses. Don't be surprised; be ready.
Gather the senses in, sit steady with your mind on what's highest. Mastery of the senses steadies wisdom.
Dwell on something and you get attached; attachment becomes wanting, and blocked wanting turns into anger.
Anger clouds judgement, clouded judgement loses memory, lost memory wrecks reason, and then you fall.
Move through the world with your senses in hand, free of grabbing and pushing away, and you find calm.
When the mind clears, sorrows start to dissolve, and understanding settles quickly.
Without inner discipline there's no clarity; without clarity, no peace; and without peace, where is happiness?
When the mind chases a wandering sense, it is swept off like a boat in the wind.
What the crowd sleeps through, the wise stay awake to. What the crowd chases, the wise see past.
I'm confused about what's right. Tell me plainly what's best; I'm ready to learn.
Rivers pour into the ocean and it stays full and still. Let desires enter you the same way.
Drop the cravings, the sense of 'mine' and the 'I' that keeps score. That's where peace is.
Rooted in this steadiness, you aren't lost, even at the very end.
Even winning everything wouldn't touch this grief that's drying me up inside.
Nourish one another, and together you'll reach the highest good.
Those who share first are freed; those who cook only for themselves feed on wrong.
One who is content and delighted in their own self has nothing left to prove.
So keep doing the work that needs doing, well and without clinging. That's how you rise.
Your advice sounds mixed and confuses me. Tell me the one thing I should do.
Janaka and others reached fulfilment through action. Keep working, if only for the good of the world.
Whatever a respected person does, others copy. The standard you set is the one people follow.
I have nothing left to gain anywhere, Krishna says, and still I keep working.
Work as hard as the ambitious do, but for everyone's good, not your own grip on results.
Don't unsettle people who are still learning by doing. Do the work well alongside them and show them.
Countless forces do the work; the ego, fooled, says 'I did it all'.
Hand your work to something higher, drop the 'mine' and the hoping, and act with the fever gone.
Even wise people move as their nature moves them. Brute suppression achieves little.
Liking and disliking lie in wait behind every sense. Don't let either take the wheel.
Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.
Why do I do the wrong thing even when I don't want to, as if something forces me?
It's desire, which turns into anger when blocked. Never satisfied, it is the real enemy here.
Like smoke over fire, dust on a mirror, desire covers your clear sight.
Desire is a fire that never gets enough. It quietly covers even the wise person's clarity.
You don't get free by not starting, and you don't get perfect by just walking away.
So start with the senses. Get them in hand, then let go of the desire that wrecks clear thinking.
Senses are strong, the mind stronger, clear judgement stronger still, and your true self strongest of all.
Knowing what is higher in you, steady yourself with yourself and defeat the desire that's hard to beat.
No one can stay without acting, even for a moment. Your nature keeps moving you.
Holding back your hands while your mind keeps feasting on the craving is self-deception.
Better: guide your senses with your mind and get to work, without being hooked.
Do the work that's yours. Doing something beats doing nothing; even living needs action.
Many have dropped craving, fear and anger, been refined by wisdom, and found their way home.
However people come to me, I meet them there. Every path, in its own way, leads to me.
What to do, what to avoid, when to hold back: the way of action is deep.
See the stillness inside activity and the activity inside stillness, and you're truly wise.
Content and leaning on no one's approval, fully busy, and yet inwardly at rest.
Expecting nothing, mind steady, letting go of possessiveness, you can work without being stained.
Content with what comes, beyond envy, steady in success and failure, you stay free even while working.
The offering, the giver, the fire, the act: see the sacred in all of it, and you reach the sacred.
Learn from those who have seen the truth: approach with humility, ask real questions, and serve.
Even if you were the worst wrongdoer of all, the raft of wisdom would carry you across.
As a blazing fire turns wood to ash, real understanding burns away the hold of past actions.
Nothing here cleanses like understanding, and with steady practice you find it within, in time.
Trust, commitment and self-control bring understanding, and understanding soon brings peace.
A mind that doubts everything finds no happiness here or anywhere.
Doubts cut away by understanding, steady within, your actions stop binding you.
Cut the doubt in your heart with clear understanding, then stand up and act.
Whenever goodness declines and wrong rises up, I come forth, Krishna promises.
To protect the good, end the harm, and set right what's broken, I appear age after age.
Like a lotus leaf in water, do your work without letting the mess soak in.
Wise people work with body, mind and heart, not for gain, but to become clearer within.
Let go of the payoff and you find lasting peace. Chase it and it chains you.
The wise see the same self in a scholar, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcast.
Those whose minds rest in evenness have already won, right here in this life.
Stepping back and acting selflessly both lead to good, but of the two, acting is better.
Don't get carried away by good news or crushed by bad. Keep your understanding steady.
Unhooked from outside pleasures, you find a joy within that doesn't run out.
Pleasures born of contact have a beginning and an end and breed sorrow. The wise don't stake their joy there.
Whoever can ride out the surge of desire and anger, here and now, is steady and happy.
Happy within, at ease within, lit from within: that person finds lasting freedom.
Doubts cut away, mind mastered, they give themselves to the good of all beings and find peace.
Senses, mind and judgement in hand, free of desire, fear and anger: that person is already free.
The divine is the well-wisher of every being, you included. Knowing this, you find peace.
The one who neither resents nor craves is the real renouncer, wherever they live.
The real renouncer does the work that's needed without leaning on its rewards, not the one who quits.
Balance isn't for those who eat too much or too little, or sleep too much or too little.
Moderate in food and rest, in work and play, in sleep and waking: that's how sorrow eases.
Like a lamp in a windless place that doesn't flicker: that's a settled mind.
When the mind finally goes still, you see yourself as you are, and you're content.
Find the gain beyond all gains, and even heavy sorrow can't shake you.
Yoga is unhooking from sorrow. Practise it with resolve and a heart that doesn't lose hope.
Little by little, with patience and steady resolve, settle the mind and let other thoughts go.
Wherever the restless mind wanders, gently bring it back. Again and again.
A calm mind, its turmoil settled, finds the highest happiness.
See yourself in every being and every being in yourself, and you see the same everywhere.
See me in everything and everything in me, and I never lose you, nor you me.
Feel others' joy and pain as if they were your own. That is the highest practice.
This calm you describe, Krishna, I can't see it lasting. My mind is too restless.
The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
Yes, the mind is restless and hard to hold. But practice and letting go can train it.
Without self-control it's hard. With sincere effort and the right means, it's within reach.
What happens to someone who believes, tries, slips, and doesn't make it to the end?
Fallen from both sides, does he scatter like a torn cloud, with nowhere to stand?
Only you can clear this doubt completely. There is no one else I can ask.
Whoever does good never comes to ruin, my friend. Not here, not after.
What you learned before isn't lost. You pick it up again and push on harder.
Past practice carries you forward, even when you don't feel like it.
The one who keeps at it, steadily, over a long time, gets there.
Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
Master yourself and you become your own best friend. Don't, and your own mind works against you like an enemy.
Self-mastered and calm, you stay centred in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, praise and insult.
To the settled mind, a lump of earth, a stone and a bar of gold are worth the same.
Friend, enemy, stranger, relative, saint or wrongdoer: the one who sees all with an even mind stands highest.
Keep your mind attached to me, lean on me, keep practising. You will come to know me fully.
In the strong, I am strength without greed or grasping. In all, I am desire that stays within what's right.
This tangle is hard to get through. Those who take shelter in me get through it.
People turn to the divine in distress, in curiosity, in need, or in wisdom. All four are welcome.
Everyone who turns to me, even in need, is noble. The one who loves me is my very self.
Whatever form someone chooses to worship with faith, I make that faith steady.
From the pull of want and push of dislike comes the confusion that traps every being.
Everything is strung on me like pearls on a single thread.
For the one who keeps remembering me, I am easy to reach.
Whatever you keep thinking about shapes who you become, right to the end.
So remember the divine at all times, and keep doing your work.
With a mind trained by practice and not wandering elsewhere, you reach what you meditate on.
I am the father of this world, and its mother, and the one who holds it all up.
I am your goal, your support, your witness, your home, your shelter and your friend.
Turn to me with your whole heart, and I will carry what you lack and guard what you have.
A leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water: whatever is offered with love, I accept.
Whatever you do, eat, give or endure, do it as an offering.
I am the same towards all; no one is hated, no one favoured. Those who love me live in me.
Even if you've done great wrong, the moment you turn wholeheartedly, count yourself among the good.
Such a person soon turns good and finds lasting peace. Mark it: no one devoted to me is ever lost.
Fix your mind on me, love me, honour me, bow to me. Joined this way, you come to me.
As the wind, wherever it blows, always rests in the sky, all beings rest in me.
Weigh the outcome before you act. Rash deeds leave a thorn that burns for years.
Dive deep, climb high, master every skill: what is not meant to be still will not happen.
The world is lit, here and there, by people poor in harsh words and rich in kind ones.
Turn a torch upside down and its flame still rises. Steadiness survives humiliation.
Better to roam wild hills with animals than to live in a palace among fools.
Learning is wealth no thief can see. It grows when you give it away and never perishes.
Fate can take away the swan's lake. It cannot take its gift of telling milk from water.
Jewellery wears out. Well-chosen speech is the one ornament that lasts.
In a foreign land, what you have learned is your family: a treasure no one can see.
With patience, who needs armour? With anger, who needs enemies? With a true friend, who needs medicine?
Good company clears the mind, puts truth in your speech and lifts your spirit. What does it not do?
A good child, a loving spouse, a kind boss, a true friend, a mind at ease: count these as grace.
Harm no one, take nothing that isn't yours, speak truly, give in time, cut craving, be kind to all.
Some never start for fear of obstacles; some quit when obstacles hit. The best keep going.
Don't beg favours from the wicked or money from a struggling friend. Stand tall in hard times.
The ignorant can be taught and the expert persuaded. The half-knower not even God can convince.
The dog grovels before whoever feeds it. The elephant waits with quiet dignity.
You can pull a gem from a crocodile's jaws, but you cannot change a mind that has dug in.
Same person, same mind, same voice. Lose money, and people suddenly treat you as someone else.
Have money and suddenly you are wise, well-born and charming. All virtues seem to lodge in gold.
Affection fades with distance, friendship without warmth, wealth with carelessness, a child with spoiling.
